detail.abstract: This essay analyzes President Donald J. Trump's Executive Order of August 7, 2025, directing the DOL to permit defined contribution retirement plans to invest in alternative assets, with Bitcoin emerging as the most consequential inclusion. The order integrates digital assets-particularly Bitcoin-alongside private equity, real estate, and infrastructure within 401(k) plans, positioning cryptocurrency not as speculative novelty but as legitimate retirement capital. Situating the order within Trump's broader crypto architecture-including prohibition of a central bank digital currency, creation of a Strategic Bitcoin Reserve, and enactment of the GENIUS, CLARITY, and Anti-CBDC Acts-the essay argues this regulatory shift constitutes a coherent strategy to embed Bitcoin within America's retirement system while modernizing fiduciary standards and reshaping U.S. capital formation. The result is a rebalanced fiduciary regime extending ERISA's economic logic to accommodate Bitcoin's uncorrelated returns, inflationhedging properties, and monetary sovereignty implications, fundamentally altering both retirement finance and macroeconomic architecture.

title: The Soaring Co-Pilot Reframing Accessible Personal Flight as an Autonomy Problem, Not an Energy Problem Working paper, July 2026
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: The Soaring Co-Pilot Reframing Accessible Personal Flight as an Autonomy Problem, Not an Energy Problem Working paper, July 2026
detail.abstract: Accessible personal flight is commonly described as awaiting a breakthrough in energy storage. This paper argues that the framing conflates two separable barriers. The first is energetic: worn and small electric aircraft cannot carry enough energy for more than minutes of flight. The second is a barrier of skill: soaring gliders remain aloft for hours by extracting energy from rising air, but locating and centering thermals is a perceptual-motor skill that conventionally takes years to master. Soaring circumvents the energetic barrier by construction, leaving the skill barrier, which is increasingly tractable to automation. Drawing together two literatures not previously connected for this purpose, field-validated autonomous thermal soaring on unmanned gliders, and Simplified Vehicle Operations (SVO) from the electric-vertical-takeoff domain, we propose the soaring co-pilot: a staged system that begins as an advisory aid coaching a pilot to work lift and advances, along a defined ladder, toward human-supervised autonomous soaring on a selflaunching micro-glider. We situate the concept against mature prior art in soaring instrumentation and crowd-sourced thermal mapping, and argue that its contribution lies in reframing the problem and in the advisory-to-autonomous trajectory rather than in any single instrument. We specify sensing and algorithmic requirements, state the argument as a set of falsifiable hypotheses, propose an evaluation methodology, and analyze the boundary between advice and control authority. The central claim is deliberately bounded: weather-permitting, longendurance personal soaring flight with a reduced skill burden is reachable without an energystorage breakthrough, and that its remaining hard problem is one of autonomy and human factors, bounded importantly by weather. We also set out a materials, durability, and systemintegrity research agenda for the hardware stages, and argue it should proceed in parallel with, not gate, the software effort. Beyond the reframing, we specify a candidate control-and-safety method, discriminating intended thermalling from incipient loss of control, and managing control-authority transitions in a regime with no benign default, and we ground the learnability claim in the motor-learning literature, specifying a faded, skill-linked coaching method whose central risk, dependence, is itself a testable prediction. Finally, we ground the concept in how large birds achieve long-distance flight, by harvesting atmospheric energy rather than by muscle, and frame the co-pilot as the engineered analogue of a soaring bird's instinct for reading the air.

title: Passing the Parcel? Banking Relationships at the Onset of Financial Distress
affiliations: Paris School of Business, ESCP-Europe and ESCP Europe

detail.title: Passing the Parcel? Banking Relationships at the Onset of Financial Distress
detail.abstract: This paper examines how banks adjust their lending strategies as borrowers approach default. Using credit registry data on French private firms, we document that long-standing lenders gradually reduce their exposure well in advance, while the number of lending relationships continues to rise until roughly one year before the default event. This pattern reflects a reallocation of credit in which new, less-informed lenders take a growing share of financing as incumbents scale back. Consistent with a model in which uninformed banks compete to refinance loans granted by better-informed lenders, these effects are more pronounced when borrowers benefit from better third-party credit ratings or higher collateral availability. The results show that private information in lending creates an exit advantage, especially when favorable public signals or collateral make refinancing feasible.

title: The Ghostwriter Problem: Generative AI, Agency Reasoning, and The Attribution Gap in NEPA Review
affiliations: Emory University School of Law

detail.title: The Ghostwriter Problem: Generative AI, Agency Reasoning, and The Attribution Gap in NEPA Review
detail.abstract:
One administrative law issue raised by generative AI may be more fundamental than the accuracy of its outputs. Administrative law has long permitted courts to infer from a formally complete administrative record that the reasons offered as the basis for a decision have been reviewed and adopted by the agency. Generative AI weakens this evidentiary relationship: it can generate complete, coherent, and technically sound substantive analyses, yet these characteristics alone do not establish that the analysis has been institutionally adopted by the agency.

This Article refers to the resulting problem as the “attribution gap.” Reliability concerns whether the analysis is credible; attribution concerns whether the administrative record sufficiently demonstrates that the agency has reviewed and institutionally adopted the material AI-generated analysis on which it relies. While existing research has addressed several related issues, this Article’s contribution is to isolate attribution as a distinct, administrative-record-based inquiry within administrative law.

This Article further argues that although Chenery, State Farm, and NEPA’s hard-look doctrine do not explicitly establish a separate form of “attribution review,” they share an institutional premise: the reasons reviewed by a court are reasons the agency has adopted. Generative AI makes that premise newly contestable, but courts can examine it through objective evidence in the administrative record without probing officials’ subjective mental processes.

The issue is especially important after Seven County, because judicial deference to an agency’s technical and methodological judgments presupposes the existence of a judgment attributable to the agency. Generative AI therefore compels administrative law to confront a more fundamental question: When formally complete administrative reasons can be generated without a corresponding institutional decision-making process, what exactly can the administrative record still demonstrate?

title: Wearable-Driven Distributed AI for Smart Pilgrimage Logistics and Pilgrim Experience during Hajj and Umrah: A Framework, Architecture, and Edge-Fog-Cloud Evaluation
affiliations: Islamic University of Madinah, Islamic University of Madinah, Islamic University of Madinah, University of Jeddah, Islamic University of Madinah and Islamic University of Madinah - Faculty of Computer and Information Systems

detail.title: Wearable-Driven Distributed AI for Smart Pilgrimage Logistics and Pilgrim Experience during Hajj and Umrah: A Framework, Architecture, and Edge-Fog-Cloud Evaluation
detail.abstract: Hajj and Umrah are among the world's largest recurring mass gatherings, creating significant challenges for healthcare delivery, crowd management, resource allocation, and service logistics. Traditional centralized monitoring systems often struggle in densely populated pilgrimage environments due to communication bottlenecks, latency, and scalability limitations. This paper presents a distributed intelligence framework that integrates wearable sensing, anomaly detection, large language models (LLMs), and hierarchical edge-fogcloud computing to improve situational awareness, support healthcare and service logistics, and enable adaptive service delivery during Hajj and Umrah. The framework combines physiological, behavioural, location, and environmental data from wearable devices with intelligence distributed across edge, fog, and cloud resources. Anomaly detection, statistical analysis, and LLM-enabled reasoning transform sensor observations into operational insights and recommendations. A real-world wearable dataset collected over seven months during visits to the Prophet's Mosque is used to demonstrate the feasibility of datadriven monitoring and context-aware intelligence generation. An edge-fog-cloud simulation environment evaluates communication overhead, energy consumption, response time, and operational responsiveness under different workload placement strategies. Results show that distributed intelligence reduces communication costs and improves responsiveness while maintaining scalable operation. The proposed framework supports pilgrimage logistics through enhanced healthcare services, crowd management, resource planning, and operational decision-making.

title: Net Systemic Value: Measuring the Downstream Value AI Agents Create and Destroy

detail.title: Net Systemic Value: Measuring the Downstream Value AI Agents Create and Destroy
detail.abstract: An AI agent inside a firm optimizes a local objective it can measure and report, and improves it. Whether the firm is better off is a different question, and a structural one: the cost of a local improvement often lands downstream, on the units the agent serves, where the agent's own measurement cannot see it. We define Net Systemic Value (NSV) of a part as the value it creates for the parts it serves minus the value it destroys within them, over a period, net of its own cost, scored from the realized outcomes of those served parts rather than from the part's self-report. NSV is the successor to Economic Value Added for a networked, AI-augmented firm: where EVA charges profit for the capital a unit consumes, NSV charges a part for the value it destroys in the units it serves. NSV consolidates without double counting only under a no-interaction/modularity condition on shared external receivers; without that condition, group NSV must be measured directly at the group boundary. We place a value-observability frontier on how much systemic value is visible at what measurement cost. The downstream effect is a treatment effect whose counterfactual is not identifiable from observational logs alone, so the defensible deliverable is a bounded estimate with a sensitivity band and periodic holdout calibration, not a single audited figure. We frame the AI Suboptimal Optimum, local metric up while NSV is negative, as a measurable dollar object that producer-side attribution (process mining, agent-ROI) and marginalcontribution estimators structurally miss, and distinguish the contribution from each.

title: Hybrid Prudential Reserves and Tokenized Capital for DAO-Based Credit Issuance

detail.title: Hybrid Prudential Reserves and Tokenized Capital for DAO-Based Credit Issuance

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial or personal interests that could have influenced the development, analysis, or conclusions of this paper.

detail.abstract: Lending protocols in decentralized finance have traditionally relied on over-collateralization mechanisms, where investor protection is primarily ensured through the automatic liquidation of collateral. While effective from an operational perspective, this approach limits the economic role of credit when compared with under-collateralized structures. In such settings, the prudential management of credit risk becomes a central element for protocol sustainability. This paper proposes a prudential framework for decentralized lending protocols by introducing an additional protection layer based on the distinction between tokenized loss-absorbing capital, an operational buffer, and a prudential reserve. The model defines three classes of subordinated instruments-First Loss Token, Contingent Capital Token, and Subordinated Backstop Token-arranged according to a progressive loss waterfall. The model is first applied to public data from Goldfinch and then extended to a TrueFi dataset, with the aim of assessing the ability of the policy to reduce losses borne by senior liquidity providers. The model shows a net reduction in losses. The sensitivity analysis confirms that the mechanism maintains a positive net benefit across variations in instrument costs, risk weights, and loss severity. The results suggest that an explicit prudential layer may contribute to strengthening the resilience of DAO-based credit protocols by making the prudential cost of risk-taking more transparent and by distinguishing between available liquidity, loss-absorbing capital, and protective reserves.

title: Parallel Institutions for Inventions: A Soviet Lesson for Expanding Sovereignty under TRIPS
affiliations: University of Warwick

detail.title: Parallel Institutions for Inventions: A Soviet Lesson for Expanding Sovereignty under TRIPS
detail.abstract: This chapter responds to the theme of sovereignty and dependence in intellectual property rights by introducing the concept of "parallel institutions," examined from empirical and normative perspectives. It argues that parallel institutions are a largely overlooked strategy of national sovereignty in the regulation of innovation markets. This argument is developed in two steps. First, the concept of parallel institutions is situated within a broader discussion on legal pluralism and the policy space that states retain under the TRIPS Agreement. Second, the chapter illustrates this concept through the Soviet regulation of inventions, which managed inventor's certificates and patents as parallel institutions. The chapter's underlying idea is that parallel institutions widen the range of instruments available to actors in the national innovation system, allowing states to tailor innovation policy within the existing international framework.

title: Masked at the Mean: Racial Wage Disparities Across the Earnings Distribution in European Soccer
affiliations: Hong Kong University of Science & Technology (HKUST) - Department of Finance

detail.title: Masked at the Mean: Racial Wage Disparities Across the Earnings Distribution in European Soccer
detail.abstract: This paper investigates racial wage disparities across the earnings distribution by examining the labor market for European professional soccer players. Utilizing professional sports as an empirical laboratory with objective performance metrics, I analyze how discrimination varies across different tiers of player income. Crucially, while standard mean-based regressions reveal no statistically significant racial wage gap on average, analyzing the entire earnings distribution paints a different picture. Through both quantile regression and individual fixed-effects analyses, I document a "crossover" effect: Black players face a significant wage discount at the lower end of the earnings distribution but command a wage premium at the top. This pattern is consistent with the "higher-standard" hypothesis of discrimination, suggesting that minority workers face an elevated evaluation threshold to achieve top-tier compensation. Consequently, only those with exceptional productivity are able to clear this higher threshold and reach the top of the earnings distribution.

title: Micro Shocks and Macro Fluctuations in the Information Network
affiliations: Yale University - Department of Economics, , Zhejiang University - College of Economics and Harbin Institute of Technology

detail.title: Micro Shocks and Macro Fluctuations in the Information Network
detail.abstract: In this paper, we study how heterogeneity in firms' attention allocation amplifies micro-level shocks into aggregate economic fluctuations. Empirically, using data on firms' browsing of one another's electronic filings on EDGAR, we document that the attention received by firms follows a fat-tailed distribution. A small subset of firms attracts a disproportionately large share of attention, consistent with our finding that the browsing-weighted measure of firm sales growth exhibits substantial predictive power for survey-based macroeconomic forecasts. Theoretically, we extend the classical dispersed-information framework to incorporate asymmetric firm-level attention through a directed graph. We derive conditions under which granular effects emerge even when firms are homogeneous in size, and we analyze how attention heterogeneity interacts with firm-size heterogeneity in magnifying micro-level shocks. Quantitatively, we find that attention heterogeneity alone can generate sizable aggregate fluctuations from micro-level shocks, and the extent to which attention asymmetry complements firm-size heterogeneity depends critically on the cross-sectional alignment between attention and firm size.

title: Procedural Environmental Rights as Crucial Tools for Environmental Justice: An Indian Perspective
affiliations: and Himachal Pradesh National Law University

detail.title: Procedural Environmental Rights as Crucial Tools for Environmental Justice: An Indian Perspective

publicationDetails.detailsText: HPNLU Journal of Environment and Disaster Management, Volume - III 2022 ISSN: 2583-1429

detail.abstract: The concept of Environmental Justice embraces the principle that all people and communities are entitled to equal protection of environmental laws as well as an equal share in environmental goods and bad. Traditionally considered a part of social justice, this concept emerged as an independent principle and movement in the 1980s and early 1990s as a result of Environmental Justice movements initiated by Asian, African, and Native American communities. Environmental Justice entails two sets of environmental rights: Substantive and Procedural environmental rights. Substantive environmental rights include a clean environment, healthy ecosystem biodiversity, etc. Procedural Environmental Rights often refer to the rights related to the procedures and processes involved in environmental decision-making, public participation, and access to information. These rights aim to ensure that individuals and communities have the opportunity to be involved in environmental matters that may affect them. Hence, are equally important. The author of this article has analyzed the Procedural dimensions of environmental justice with special reference to India. The article is divided into five parts. Partone provides a conceptual understanding of the topic. Part two contains a discussion on the global history of environmental justice followed by part three which discusses the Indian perspective on environmental justice. In the fourth part an analysis has been made of the role of Procedural environmental rights in achieving environmental justice in India followed by a conclusion in part fifth of this Article

title: Manufacturing Flow Management (MFM): A Decision Framework for Production Managers to Improve Operational Flow, Capacity, and Business Performance

detail.title: Manufacturing Flow Management (MFM): A Decision Framework for Production Managers to Improve Operational Flow, Capacity, and Business Performance

detail.abstract:
This white paper introduces the Manufacturing Flow Management (MFM) Framework, a practical decision-making methodology designed to help Production Managers improve operational flow, effective capacity, inventory alignment, customer service, and business performance. The framework was developed from practical manufacturing leadership experience across multiple production environments and addresses a recurring gap in operations management: how production leaders should prioritize decisions when business demand, operational constraints, resource limitations, and performance indicators compete simultaneously.

The MFM Framework proposes that production decisions should follow a structured sequence: understand business demand, validate operational reality, protect operational flow, build future capacity, and measure business outcomes. Rather than maximizing local efficiency or individual KPIs, the framework emphasizes business-driven decision-making, operational stability, hidden capacity recovery, and the alignment of production execution with customer demand.

The paper presents implementation guidance, common operational mistakes, practical case scenarios, evidence from manufacturing practice, and leadership principles for Production Managers. It argues that sustainable operational excellence is achieved not merely through better metrics, additional resources, or advanced planning systems, but through consistently making better operational decisions in the correct order.

title: Energy in Production Functions: A Cautionary Note and a Reply to the Critics
affiliations: De La Salle University and Unaffiliated Author

detail.title: Energy in Production Functions: A Cautionary Note and a Reply to the Critics

keywords: Accounting Identity Critique of Production Functions

detail.abstract: Ecological economists have long argued that energy is a quantitatively more important factor of production than what its cost share of about 0.04-0.10 implies, and have sought to prove it by augmenting the aggregate production function with energy, reporting output elasticities between 0.20 and 0.76. We argue that this empirical strategy is self-defeating. While the conceptual claim-that no production occurs without energy-is correct, it cannot be shown by estimating an energy-augmented aggregate production function. Doing so conflicts with a fundamental insight of ecological economics, for it treats two ontologically distinct categories as symmetric: labor and capital are funds that render a service and leave the process intact, while energy and materials are flows that are transformed and used up. Two further critiques reinforce this conclusion: the aggregation literature shows that the conditions for an aggregate production function with neoclassical properties to exist are hardly met by actual economies; and the accounting-identity critique shows that production function regressions merely approximate the national accounting identity, with its coefficients tending toward the factor shares, not necessarily equal to the true elasticities. The gap between estimated energy elasticities and energy's cost share is just a feature of this algebra. The conclusion is methodological: ecological economics should rely on biophysical accounting-input-output analysis, MuSIASEM, exergy/useful-work accounting used descriptively, and stock-flow consistent biophysical macro models-rather than on a search for the elusive output elasticity of energy.

title: Strategic Engagement and Legal Pluralism: Navigating Knowledge and Expertise in Mining Disputes

detail.title: Strategic Engagement and Legal Pluralism: Navigating Knowledge and Expertise in Mining Disputes

The article also draws heavily from my doctoral dissertation entitled, “The implications of legal pluralism to understanding mining conflicts: a socio-legal study of Thailand’s Chatree gold mine,” and previous work conducted in relation to a 2023 conference on critical minerals and circular economy hosted by the Asia Research Institute, National University of Singapore.

detail.abstract: This article explores how community and civil society actors in mining conflicts strategically engage with legal and technical vocabularies to assert legitimacy, contest exclusion, and influence mining governance. Drawing on an empirical case study of Thailand's Chatree gold mine, the article analyzes how affected groups navigate overlapping normative systems, such as state law, transnational norms, and technocratic discourses, through informal learning and strategic appropriation of expert language. Framed through the conceptual lens of legal pluralism, the study highlights how actors interpret and mobilize diverse normative orders to articulate grievances, shape narratives, and attempt to gain access to decision-making spaces. These engagements unfold across scalar dimensions, from local to international levels, reflecting both selective alignment with, and resistance to, dominant legal and institutional frameworks. By foregrounding norm contestation and plural authority, the article contributes to socio-legal scholarship on resource conflict, illustrating how actors operate in contexts of institutional distrust to advance alternative visions of justice, development, and legitimacy in sites of mineral resource development.

title: A Review of Efficient Routing Architectures Using OSPF, BGP, and MPLS in Multi-Protocol Networks
affiliations: Infogain Corporation

detail.title: A Review of Efficient Routing Architectures Using OSPF, BGP, and MPLS in Multi-Protocol Networks
detail.abstract: Protocol networks are the frameworks in digital communication and establish the requisite principles, structures and mechanisms according to which data is relayed, directed and accepted throughout intricate and connected systems. The networks take advantage of a mixture of routing and forwarding protocols to realize important aims like efficiency, reliability, scale, as well as responsiveness to dynamic conditions. The paper gives an in-depth discussion of three major protocols, which form the basis of the functioning of contemporary IPbased networks, which are Open Shortest Path First (OSPF), Border Gateway Protocol (BGP), and Multiprotocol Label Switching (MPLS). The protocols are individually studied with regard to their architecture, working principles, core concepts, and real applications on a network of enterprises, as well as very massive service providers. Besides the analysis of the protocol itself, the paper also explores the heterogeneity of the protocol interoperability in the heterogeneous network environment, focusing on the most important issues related to the integration and coexistence.

title: Towards a Generative Relational Theory of Subject Formation

detail.title: Towards a Generative Relational Theory of Subject Formation
detail.abstract: The study of early development ordinarily takes the subject as given and traces the capacities it acquires. This paper takes the prior question as its object, namely how a subject is formed at all, and argues that the subject is the relational outcome of development rather than its starting point. It carries forward a research programme that has replaced the individual with generative relational being and the sign with a generative relational epistemology, and it now replaces the cognitive ability, as the unit of analysis in early development, with the relational capacity. Generative relational capacity is defined as the capacity to enter, sustain, transform, and reproduce shared relational fields, and the classic findings of developmental research, joint attention, gaze following, social referencing, and theory of mind, are reread as empirical manifestations of one developing capacity rather than as discrete cognitive modules, with the attributions called theory of mind and the earlier scene of joint attention taken as showings of the same capacity in different registers. The account is then opened onto its social-ecological condition. Subject formation proceeds within a relational ecology, the historically and culturally organized configuration that makes some relational fields possible while constraining others, and is never a sealed dyadic affair. A comparative note on institutional childcare sets three grammars of relational-field formation beside one another, and finds in each a distinct configuration of achievement and cost, with no one of them a model. On this basis the political economy of subject formation is restated. Capital does not shape the child directly; it reconfigures the relational ecology, and its most recent frontier, beyond the extraction of value from the sign and from relation, is an invasion of the generative process itself, a reach that damages the formation of a subject together with its own subsequent power to generate. The account closes, in the manner it requires of itself, on the questions that a generative developmental psychology would have to take up.

title: Policing Expressive Governance: A Framework for Judicial Review of Executive Viewpoint Retaliation
affiliations: Loyola Law School Los Angeles

detail.title: Policing Expressive Governance: A Framework for Judicial Review of Executive Viewpoint Retaliation

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No personal or financial relationship with other people or organizations.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable.
declarations.funderStatement: Nobody funded this research.

detail.abstract:
The gravest contemporary threats to expressive freedom increasingly take the form not of statutes or criminal sanctions but of procurement decisions, grant terminations, security-clearance revocations, and regulatory designations — the discretionary instruments of executive administration. When the executive deploys these instruments to penalize disfavored viewpoints while preserving the appearance of ordinary governance, it engages in what I have elsewhere called expressive governance. The phenomenon is doctrinally elusive because it operates in domains where courts have long extended substantial deference to executive judgment, and because its defining features — facial neutrality, discretion, and post hoc justification — obscure the very motive the retaliation inquiry must locate.

This essay argues that existing First Amendment doctrine supplies the governing principles but lacks an administrable method calibrated to the low-visibility, discretion-cloaked form the problem now assumes, and it proposes such a method: three interlocking tools. First, a clear-statement requirement asks whether Congress authorized applying the discretionary instrument to domestic expressive activity or its infrastructure at all — a question of statutory reach, not of authority to discriminate by viewpoint, which Congress cannot confer. Second, a burden-shifting rule, triggered only by a conjunctive showing of a viewpoint-linked pattern and an exploitable dependency relationship, requires the government to prove on the record that it would have taken the same action for viewpoint-neutral reasons. Third, a presumption of systemic distortion heightens what the government must produce where the target is an expressive intermediary — an effect of burden allocation, not a new tier of scrutiny.

The essay develops the framework through the pending litigation over the Department of War's supply-chain-risk designation of a leading artificial-intelligence company, and tests it against the law-firm executive orders, public-broadcasting funding rescissions, press-credential revocations, and public employment and hiring. The method is politically symmetric by design: it operates on burden allocation and record evidence, gives the government a genuine path to prevail where its reasons are real, and equips courts to distinguish legitimate discretionary administration from viewpoint retaliation conducted through the routine machinery of the administrative state.

title: The Paradox of Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism: Evaluating the “Downstream Loophole” and Its Impact on Eu Manufacturing Competitiveness (2023–2026)

detail.title: The Paradox of Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism: Evaluating the “Downstream Loophole” and Its Impact on Eu Manufacturing Competitiveness (2023–2026)
detail.abstract: The European Union's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) was established under the European Green Deal to mitigate carbon leakage and protect domestic producers facing compliance costs under the EU Emissions Trading System (ETS). However, the practical application of CBAM is severely undermined by a structural disparity in its legislative scope. While CBAM puts carbon tariffs on primary precursors-such as unwrought aluminium (CN code 7601)-it exempts complex downstream products, including aluminium alloy wheels (CN code 8708 70 50). This study evaluates the "downstream loophole," arguing that taxing raw inputs while leaving out finished components penalizes domestic mid-stream manufacturers and stimulates the obstruction of climate rules. Analyzing monthly Eurostat trade data (ext_st_easitc) from late 2025 into early 2026, the paper shows that nearly €79 billion worth of finished machinery and transport equipment consistently enters the EU market each month without facing any carbon adjustments. Furthermore, an evaluation of the 2026 legislative response (COM(2025) 989 final and COM(2025) 87 final) reveals that while the European Commission has formally recognized these structural gaps and proposed a downstream extension, the two-year implementation delay until 2028 creates a critical period of vulnerability. This policy gap risks accelerating capital flight and permanently weakening the EU's manufacturing base.

title: Decolonizing Community Engagement: Operationalizing Pakikipagkapwa as a Relational Framework within the Canadian Diaspora

detail.title: Decolonizing Community Engagement: Operationalizing Pakikipagkapwa as a Relational Framework within the Canadian Diaspora
detail.abstract: Current Equity, Diversity, and Inclusion (EDI) practices and public consultation models within Canadian institutional, municipal, and social service sectors frequently rely on top-down, bureaucratic, and transactional methodologies. These Western-centric approaches often relegate immigrant, migrant, and diaspora communities to passive data sources, failing to build deep, sustainable trust. This paper introduces a novel, culturally responsive alternative by adapting Pakikipagkapwa—a foundational concept from Sikolohiyang Pilipino (Filipino Psychology) signifying a "shared inner self" and deep interconnectedness—into a structured community engagement framework designed specifically for the Canadian context. The paper operationalizes the original eight-level scale of Filipino interpersonal interaction, tracing a methodological progression from outsider status (Ibang-Tao) characterized by surfacelevel civility (Pakikitungo), to trusted insider status (Hindi Ibang-Tao) culminating in absolute mutual respect and shared human identity (Pakikipagkapwa). By translating these cultural tenets into actionable, field-ready checklists and participatory methods—such as Pakikipagkwentuhan (epistemic storytelling circles)—this framework provides Canadian community organizers, researchers, and policymakers with a concrete tool to transcend performative diversity metrics. Critically, the paper argues that shifting from extractive consultation to relational accountability not only decolonizes community development practices but also reorients the very measure of engagement success: from quantifiable outputs to the depth of relational integration and mutual empowerment. This reframing carries profound implications for how Canadian institutions conceptualize evidence, allocate resources, and ultimately honor their commitments to multiculturalism and genuine reconciliation with marginalized diaspora groups.

title: Business Cycles of China's Housing Oversupply
affiliations: Texas State University, San Marcos - Department of Finance and Economics and University of New Hampshire

detail.title: Business Cycles of China's Housing Oversupply
detail.abstract: In the early 2000s, China experienced an extraordinary expansion in its housing sector. In 2016, for instance, housing-related activities accounted for nearly 29% of GDP. Despite slowing population growth and declining absorption rates, housing construction continued at a rapid pace, resulting in substantial inventories of unsold housing units across many Chinese cities. This paper introduces search-and-matching frictions in the housing market to the stochastic dynamic general equilibrium (DSGE) model to study the business cycle features of China's housing oversupply. The model is estimated using a rich set of Chinese quarterly data from 2004Q4 to 2023Q4 within a Bayesian framework. The estimated model successfully replicates the observed volatilities of housing variables, including housing prices, housing investment, and inventories of unsold units. The model also captures well the comovement between the housing market variables and the aggregate economy seen in the data. Our variance decomposition exercises show that shocks to housing productivity and buyers' search attempts are the primary sources of fluctuations in China's housing market.

reference: Pierre Larouche, "Regulatory Space and 21st-Century Dynamics", Chapter 1 in Panos Delimatsis ad Giorgio Monti, eds., EU Law and Regulatory Spaces, Essays in Honour of Leigh Hancher (Bloomsbury, 2026).
title: Regulatory Space and 21st Century Dynamics
affiliations: Université de Montréal

detail.title: Regulatory Space and 21st Century Dynamics

publicationDetails.detailsText: Pierre Larouche, "Regulatory Space and 21st-Century Dynamics", Chapter 1 in Panos Delimatsis ad Giorgio Monti, eds., EU Law and Regulatory Spaces, Essays in Honour of Leigh Hancher (Bloomsbury, 2026).

detail.abstract: This contribution revisits Leigh Hancher and Michael Moran’s Regulatory Space in view of twenty-first-century dynamics. The main elements of the regulatory space – private and public stakeholders and the space itself – have come under pressure. As regards firms, the incentives to participate in the regulatory space are no longer as self-evident as they were in Regulatory Space: faced with regulatory spaces that may not be dimensioned appropriately, global firms have disengaged and taken a more passive stance. On the side of public authorities, the main change is the emergence of independent national regulatory authorities (NRAs), out of rule of law considerations, namely impartiality and non-discrimination. NRA separation from higher-level political powers – legislative and executive – does not imply that these powers withdraw from the regulatory space, nor should it; in any event, the NRA remains accountable towards these powers through mechanisms that do not impinge on its independence. However, the rationales underpinning NRA separation do not provide any clue as to how to organise the co-existence and interplay of these two sets of public stakeholders – NRAs and higher-level powers – in the regulatory space. In particular, the concept pair of ‘policy’ and ‘implementation’ is best seen as the two ends of a continuum rather than an operational distinction. In the end, therefore, tensions remain between the respective roles and positions of NRAs and higher-level powers. In the US, these tensions are leading to a roll-back of NRA separation (which was never as strong as in the EU to start with). In the EU, these tensions can be linked with the increased tendency of the EU institutions to resort to legislation as the preferred vehicle for participation in the regulatory space. As a consequence, EU legislation is extended into regulatory intricacies, leading to legislative hubris (overreach) in the worst cases. Finally, market dynamics – induced by innovation – have reduced the distance between commercial and regulatory spaces, if not fused them altogether. For firms, regulation is an integral part of strategic management. For public authorities, access to the market knowledge of private firms is essential to keep the regulatory space relevant. In the end, firms must be more engaged, higher-level political powers must embrace an ethos of self-restraint, and commercial and regulatory spaces must be considered together.

title: The Persistence of Stock-Selection Residuals

detail.title: The Persistence of Stock-Selection Residuals

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is the founder and CEO of Blue Water Macro Corp, which develops risk modeling tools and maintains the RiskModels platform used in this research. No external funding or conflicts of interest are declared beyond this affiliation.

detail.abstract:
We define mutual-fund stock-selection skill not as a human trait but as a measurable residual: the idiosyncratic component of performance that remains after the replicable exposures modeled in this decomposition — market, sector, subsector, and Fama–French size/value — are orthogonalized away, and that exhibits cross-sectional stability under out-of-sample testing. Using a point-in-time, holdings-based architecture, we reconstruct each fund's return from the securities it actually held and strip those exposures sequentially — a position-level identification that asks whether the stock-specific return a fund *generated* persists, not whether a historical return intercept does.


The isolated stock-selection residual exhibits statistically significant out-of-sample persistence: the forward top-minus-bottom-quintile spread is about **+2.3 percentage points**, with annual non-overlapping reliability of ***t* ≈ 3.4**. When the identical point-in-time machinery is applied to style- and sector-timing components as negative-control signals, their forward predictive content does not survive; stock selection does. The differential survival supports the interpretation that the result is specific to the stock-selection residual, not a generic consequence of the validation machinery. The practical consequence is for manager diligence: conventional tools — style classification, sector allocation, benchmark-relative attribution, and recent performance — describe what a fund owned but are weak evidence of *repeatable* skill, because the standard toolkit blends stock selection with style and sector exposure rather than isolating it. A longitudinal variance decomposition localizes the persistence entirely within the *between-fund* variance — a persistent between-fund level difference, not a transient timing signal. We read the result narrowly: a robust ranking signal within a chosen mandate, not unconditional evidence that active management outperforms net of fees.

title: Subjective Risk-Return Trade-off
affiliations: The Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK) - CUHK Business School, The University of Hong Kong - Faculty of Business and Economics and The University of Hong Kong

detail.title: Subjective Risk-Return Trade-off
detail.abstract: We survey 2,548 representative U.S. respondents to estimate subjective risk-return trade-offs across savings, government bonds, stocks, real estate, gold, and cryptocurrencies. We document robust negative relationships between perceptions of risk and return among risky assets, which are observed even among financially literate respondents. Strong asset-specific sentiments, reflected in large deviations of return perceptions from average perceptions, drive these significant negative risk-return trade-offs. Both strong optimism and pessimism contribute to negative risk-return trade-offs with similar magnitudes. These negative risk-return trade-offs translate into under-diversified portfolios, as investors avoid assets they perceive to generate low returns and high risk.

title: Corporate Gender Quotas Under the Lens: Evidence from California Senate Bill No. 826
affiliations: Rowan University, Fordham University  , New York University (NYU) - Leonard N. Stern School of Business and Fordham University

detail.title: Corporate Gender Quotas Under the Lens: Evidence from California Senate Bill No. 826
detail.abstract: California Senate Bill No. 826 (SB 826) was the first binding gender quota for corporate boards in the United States. Using a difference-in-differences-in-differences design that exploits firms' differential exposure to the law, we examine its effects on corporate strategy and the representation of women in management. We find that the law was binding and led affected firms to reorient their strategy toward longer horizons, with increased investment in research and development, intangibles, organizational capital, and environmental performance, and a corporate culture more aligned with long-term values. These shifts come with the cost of lower short-term profitability. Beyond board composition, we provide evidence that the law has also increased the presence of women in other managerial positions within affected corporations and has had spillover effects on other states through firms’ internal networks of establishments. These findings suggest that the law's effects extend beyond board composition and beyond California's borders.

title: Autonomous Governance Intelligence: An AI-Native Framework for Continuous Democratic Visibility and Accountability

detail.title: Autonomous Governance Intelligence: An AI-Native Framework for Continuous Democratic Visibility and Accountability

declarations.funderStatement: Not applicable

detail.abstract: Governance intelligence should be treated as a continuous state-estimation problem rather than a complaint-resolution problem. Traditional civic technology platforms operate on transactional, complaint-centric architectures that process citizen grievances as isolated tickets. While effective for administrative workflow management, these systems often fail to generate a comprehensive understanding of broader governance conditions, disconnect citizen participation from collective impact, and prioritize procedural activity over measurable public outcomes. This paper introduces IndiaOS, a theoretical AI-native governance framework designed to transition from fragmented grievance management toward continuous governance intelligence. At the center of the framework is the Autonomous Governance Intelligence Layer (AGIL), a multi-engine architecture that continuously ingests decentralized civic observations and transforms them into structured public issues through semantic, spatial, and temporal clustering mechanisms. By establishing a clear separation between private citizen inputs and public issue outputs, the framework reduces informational fragmentation while enabling large-scale aggregation of civic signals. The model further introduces a dual-state evaluation framework that distinguishes between Official Status, representing institutional claims of resolution, and Reality Status, representing continuously verified ground-level conditions. Through multi-source evidence aggregation and dynamic accountability assessment, the architecture seeks to provide a more accurate representation of governance performance than traditional complaint-management systems. The paper argues that artificial intelligence can evolve beyond stateless generative applications toward persistent, stateful monitoring systems capable of supporting transparency, accountability, and evidence-based democratic governance. Author Ashnik X. Chaudhary is a mechanical engineering student, independent researcher, and founder exploring the application of artificial intelligence to governance, civic participation, and institutional accountability. His current work focuses on IndiaOS, an AI-native governance intelligence framework designed to transform decentralized citizen observations into continuous public visibility and evidence-based accountability systems. His broader interests include collective intelligence, digital democracy, public-sector innovation, and emerging technology policy.

title: Backfill and Survivorship Bias in Managed-Futures Databases: A Structural Critique

detail.title: Backfill and Survivorship Bias in Managed-Futures Databases: A Structural Critique
detail.abstract: Managed-futures and commodity trading advisor (CTA) performance databases are widely used by allocators and researchers to evaluate historical returns, risk-adjusted performance, and persistence. Yet these databases are structurally vulnerable to backfill bias (also called instant-history bias) and survivorship bias, which systematically inflate reported returns and understate risk. This paper synthesizes the academic literature on hedge fund and CTA database biases-notably the canonical work of Malkiel and Saha (2005), Liang (2000), Fung and Hsieh (2000), and later CTA-specific studies-and situates them within the regulatory frameworks governing performance presentation: the CFA Institute's Global Investment Performance Standards (GIPS) 2020, the SEC's Marketing Rule, and NFA/CFTC rules for CTAs. We argue that current CTA databases often fail to satisfy the valuation, composite-construction, and verification principles required by GIPS and SEC standards, particularly around the inclusion of backfilled track records and the treatment of non-surviving funds. Using a Monte Carlo simulation, we show that even modest backfill and survivorship effects can materially alter perceived alpha and Sharpe ratios. We conclude that allocators should treat unverified, backfilled CTA indices and composites as unreliable benchmarks and that regulators and industry bodies should explicitly extend GIPS-like principles to managed-futures performance databases.

title: Do Gamma-Exposure Walls Exhibit Strike-Local Effects? A Pre-Registered, Control-Matched Test of Strike-Local Dealer-Gamma Effects in SPY

detail.title: Do Gamma-Exposure Walls Exhibit Strike-Local Effects? A Pre-Registered, Control-Matched Test of Strike-Local Dealer-Gamma Effects in SPY
detail.abstract: This paper seeks to stress-test a common, prevailing narrative that aggregate near-expiry GEX 'walls' act as 1) intraday support and resistance, 2) act as magnets that pin price and 3) act as zones of suppressed volatility. The proposed mechanism, especially the concept of 'pinning', is borrowed from Ni, Pearson, and Poteshman, 2005, who shows that option market-maker delta-hedging contributes to individual stocks clustering at strike prices on monthly expiration dates. We ask whether the mechanism extends to intraday price behaviour around open-defined aggregate GEX walls in SPY, in the modern daily-expiry era. Using a pre-registered test, controls defined as rank 2-5 GEX nodes, a pipeline frozen before out-of-sample data is read, and a one-shot holdout, we test three facets of the claim: 1) break-resistance, 2) pinning (dwell), 3) volatility dampening. Across every primary facet, the wall is statistically indistinguishable from rank 2-5 GEX strikes, and this null replicates from validation to holdout. This result is invariant across both the pre-registered primary specification, testing against walls derived from net-GEX, and against analytics platform definitions, where call (put) walls are defined as the strike with the largest magnitude call (put) side of GEX. The zone contrast that excludes zero in both tiers (put-wall dwell) is traced to control geometry rather than any wall mechanism. This is consistent with gamma acting as a market-wide regime influence rather than a strike-local one.

title: Behavioral Escalation as a Single-Agent Stopping Problem: A Dynamic Discrete Choice Model of Crisis Onset in Residential Treatment

detail.title: Behavioral Escalation as a Single-Agent Stopping Problem: A Dynamic Discrete Choice Model of Crisis Onset in Residential Treatment

detail.abstract: We develop a structural model of behavioral escalation in residential treatment settings, framing the onset of critical incidents including but not limited to: self-harm, psychiatric hospitalization, and elopement, as the solution to a single-agent optimal stopping problem. A client's behavioral regulatory system accumulates costs over a discrete state space indexed by observed dysregulation, and exits regulated equilibrium when the option value of continued regulation is exhausted. Environmental catalysts, including biological family contact, legal proceedings, and placement disruptions, enter the payoff function as shifters that reduce the option value of regulation and accelerate deterioration through the state space. We motivate the model theoretically, derive its key empirical predictions, and outline an estimation strategy based on Conditional Choice Probability (CCP) methods that is feasible given the sparse incident frequencies characteristic of residential treatment data. The model generates two central testable predictions: (1) the hazard of incident onset peaks at a lag of approximately 1.5 to 2 days following observed dysregulation, consistent with a threshold-crossing process rather than acute reactivity; and (2) exposure to destabilizing environmental catalysts significantly reduces the option value of continued regulation and predicts incident onset independently of contemporaneous behavioral state. These predictions have direct implications for early intervention protocol design in behavioral healthcare settings. During the preparation of this work, the author used Claude (Anthropic) as an interactive research aid. This included identifying relevant literature on dynamic discrete choice estimation, assisting in the mathematical formalization of the model conceived by the author, and providing language editing and LATEX formatting support. The research question, conceptual framing, all modeling decisions and conclusions are the author’s own. The author takes full responsibility for the content of the manuscript.

title: Estimating the New Keynesian Phillips Curve (NKPC) with Fat-tailed Events
affiliations: Reserve Bank of India, Reserve Bank of India and Reserve Bank of India, Mumbai

detail.title: Estimating the New Keynesian Phillips Curve (NKPC) with Fat-tailed Events
detail.abstract: This paper estimates a stable, linear New Keynesian Phillips Curve (NKPC) for India, a systemically important emerging market economy (EME), that remains robust to large, unanticipated shocks such as the COVID-19 pandemic. To do so, we estimate a modified Unobserved Components Model (UCM) with an additional Student-t distributed irregular component in the trend-cycle decomposition of GDP. This successfully isolates transitory outlier shocks like COVID-19 from trend and cycle estimates. We also construct a model-based measure of inflation expectations that captures adaptive learning from a long inflation history and real-time updating during the pandemic. Based on a joint estimation of the output gap and NKPC parameters from within a Bayesian state-space, we show that accounting for fattailed events is crucial for obtaining a reliable Phillips curve in the case of emerging markets. Finally, we build a small closed-economy semi-structural macro-model for India that links monetary policy transmission channel in our fat-tail-robust NKPC and UCM framework and examines their impact on output and inflation.

title: Reproductive Rights Adjudication in Malawi: A Critical Analysis of AC (A Minor) v Jenala Solomon & Others

detail.title: Reproductive Rights Adjudication in Malawi: A Critical Analysis of AC (A Minor) v Jenala Solomon & Others
detail.abstract: In October 2025, the High Court of Malawi delivered a landmark judgment in AC (A Minor) v Jenala Solomon & Others, holding that a 14-year-old survivor of defilement was entitled to access safe abortion services under the Gender Equality Act. This article provides a comprehensive doctrinal analysis of the judgment, examining its implications for Malawi's restrictive abortion law framework. It argues that while the decision represents a significant progressive development, it also exposes the deep tensions between Malawi's Penal Code, constitutional rights, and international human rights obligations. The court's purposive interpretation of the 'preservation of life' exception to include mental health, and its recognition of an 'automatic right' to abortion for child survivors of sexual violence, marks a departure from previous judicial caution. However, the judgment's reliance on the Gender Equality Act-a statute expressly made 'subject to any other written law'-raises questions about its doctrinal foundation. The article evaluates the decision in light of comparative jurisprudence, international human rights law, and the stalled legislative reform process, concluding with recommendations for comprehensive legal and policy reform.

title: The Health Impacts of Relaxing Internal Migration Policies: Quasiexperimental Evidence from China
affiliations: , Department of Social Work, National Taiwan University, Renmin University of China and Columbia University School of Social Work

detail.title: The Health Impacts of Relaxing Internal Migration Policies: Quasiexperimental Evidence from China
detail.abstract: This study examines the health impacts of a large-scale internal migration policy reform in China. Using nationally representative data from the China Labor-Force Dynamics Survey (2012-2018) and a unique dataset on city-level policy intensity and adoption timing, we employ a triple-difference approach to estimate the effects of migration policies on migrants' perceived physical and emotional health. We find that more lenient policies significantly improve migrants' health relative to natives. Integration policies yield health benefits approximately 3-4 times greater than selection policies. The most effective policy tools enhancing all health outcomes are integration policies granting migrants access to public services and education and selection policies targeting high-skilled migrants. Health improvements are driven by reduced overtime work, greater social capital, and stronger integration with natives.

title: Nested Logit Demand for Differentiated Fuels: Station-Level Evidence on Ethanol–Gasoline Substitution in Brazil
affiliations: International Monetary Fund (IMF)

detail.title: Nested Logit Demand for Differentiated Fuels: Station-Level Evidence on Ethanol–Gasoline Substitution in Brazil
detail.abstract: ​This paper estimates a nested logit demand system for differentiated retail fuel stations in the Londrina–Cambé metropolitan area (Paraná, Brazil) over 2007–2009. In this flex-fuel setting, consumers choose both a station and a fuel (ethanol or gasoline). Because consumer origin–destination data are unavailable, spatial frictions are proxied by grouping 154 stations into six geographic nests, and demand parameters are identified using cost-shifter instruments (wholesale acquisition costs, international sugar and crude-oil prices) together with BLP-style rival-characteristic averages. Estimates yield a within-region correlation parameter that is positive and statistically significant, supporting the nested logit over the multinomial logit. Ethanol demand is substantially more sensitive to the ethanol–gasoline relative price than gasoline demand, consistent with FFV owners representing the marginal fuel-switchers in an otherwise gasoline-dominant fleet. Implied elasticities vary meaningfully across regions of the same metropolitan market: ethanol own-relative-price elasticities range from −0.05 to −0.08 across nests, with the strongest responsiveness in the Center and Cambé regions. A documented cartel episode operating during part of the sample provides institutional context for interpreting relative-price variation but is not used to identify demand parameters. The paper contributes empirical evidence on station-level fuel substitution in a major flex-fuel economy and documents within-market heterogeneity relevant for the industrial-organization literature on spatially differentiated retail markets and for the design of biofuel and fuel-tax policies.

title: Cooperative Housing, Belonging, and Mental Health -A Difference-in-Differences Analysis of the Canadian Housing Survey

detail.title: Cooperative Housing, Belonging, and Mental Health -A Difference-in-Differences Analysis of the Canadian Housing Survey
detail.abstract: This paper examines whether living in a housing cooperative buffered or amplified changes in self-rated mental health during the COVID-19 pandemic relative to residents of other housing tenure models. Using repeated cross-sections of the Canadian Housing Survey (CHS) from 2018 (pre-pandemic), 2021 (during), and 2022-23 (post-pandemic), I implement a difference-in-differences design to compare mental health trajectories for cooperative residents versus private market renters, owners, and subsidized renters. Market cooperative residents experienced significantly less mental health decline than private renters during COVID-19 (DiD = 0.235, Cohen’s d=0.22), buffered from approximately 72% of the mental health decline experienced by private renters. This effect exceeded the baseline mental health premium associated with homeownership, which provided no significant difference in protection during the crisis. Cooperative residents also reported a dramatic surge in community belonging during COVID-19, the largest among long-tenure residents, while simultaneously facing greater relative economic hardship.  This points to social connection rather than financial buffering as the operative mechanism in explaining these differences.  These findings suggest that housing tenure is an institutional condition shaping mental health resilience in the face of population-wide stressors, and that the cooperative tenure model’s built-in social infrastructure may provide protective resources.

title: A Quantitative Signature of Cooperative Housing-Discriminant Analysis of Housing-Related Stressor Dimensions Across Household Types

detail.title: A Quantitative Signature of Cooperative Housing-Discriminant Analysis of Housing-Related Stressor Dimensions Across Household Types
detail.abstract:
Housing research has long relied on a binary distinction between owning and renting, obscuring meaningful variation along the spectrum of tenure models.  This paper argues that housing tenure models are better understood as a multidimensional institutional arrangement that varies in its permeability to stressors, the degree to which a given tenure model allows adverse housing-related physical, economic, psychological, and social conditions to penetrate and accumulate in residents' lived experience.  Drawing on Pearlin et al.’s (1981) stress process model and a biopsychosocial framework, I hypothesized that cooperative housing, through its cost-based rent structure, autonomous democratic governance, and resident-centered organizational design, constitutes a tenure model that is, both qualitatively and quantitatively, less permeable to housing stressors than private rental housing.

Using data from the 2018 Canadian Housing Survey (Statistics Canada, 2018), this study utilizes exploratory factor analysis (EFA) to identify the latent dimensional structure underlying condition, satisfaction, experience, and social connection variables and linear discriminant analysis (LDA) to characterize the multivariate “signature” distinguishing market cooperative from private rental housing, both in a pooled sample and stratified by household type.  EFA identified nine interpretable dimensions of rental housing experience consistent with a genuinely multidimensional structure in which no single dimension dominates and consistent with conceptualizing these dimensions as chronic stressors that are cumulative in the lives of residents.  In comparison, the overall cooperative signature was defined primarily by greater adequacy of dwelling space and reduced economic hardship-coping behaviors.  The stratified analyses revealed substantial heterogeneity by household type.  Affordability crossed the small-effect threshold for all four household types investigated in this study, indicating a consistent institutional advantage rather than a context-dependent one.  Physical condition favored cooperative residents most strongly for families with children.  Tenure stability was strongest for couples without children.  Single persons exhibited the broadest signature, with advantages distributed across four dimensions and consistent with cumulative chronic stressor exposure on a single income.  Across all strata, cooperative housing scored at least as well as other housing types on every dimension. 

These findings suggest that a cooperative housing advantage exists and operates through institutional mechanisms inherent in the tenure model, with implications for housing policy and the measurement of more healthful housing for residents.

detail.abstract: This study examines aviation as an instrument of soft power in international relations, focusing on the United Arab Emirates and the State of Qatar. It introduces the concept of "transit globalisation" — the process by which states leverage geographic location and aviation networks to convert connectivity into sustained symbolic and geopolitical gains. Using a qualitative comparative case study approach, this research analyses Qatar Airways and Emirates as state-backed "flying ambassadors," examining their strategies through state support, network expansion, narrative construction, and crisis management. The findings show that Qatar Airways prioritises geopolitical adaptability and legitimacy, evident in its response to the 2017 Gulf Blockade and the COVID-19 pandemic, while Emirates reflects the UAE's ambitions of geoeconomic expansion and prestige, positioning Dubai as a central node in global connectivity. This dissertation establishes aviation diplomacy as a significant and emerging component of statecraft, demonstrating how infrastructure, mobility, and branding generate soft power, and calls for further research to expand this field.

title: Does Energy Poverty Dim the Future? Energy Deprivation and Forward-Looking Expectations in South Africa1
affiliations: University of Cape Town and University of Cape Town

detail.title: Does Energy Poverty Dim the Future? Energy Deprivation and Forward-Looking Expectations in South Africa1
detail.abstract: A large literature shows that energy poverty lowers present welfare, but its consequences for how individuals view their future are largely unexamined. Using five waves (2008–2017) of South Africa's National Income Dynamics Study (NIDS), we estimate the effect of household multidimensional energy poverty on two forward-looking outcomes: expected household income in five years and the intention to relocate within two years. Controlling for individual and wave fixed effects, we find that a one-unit increase in the energy-poverty score lowers expected future income by 0.40 standard deviations and raises the intention to relocate by 0.26 standard deviations. A within-fixed-effects Gelbach (2016) decomposition shows that observed resource, health and present-wellbeing channels account for only about one-sixth of the income-expectation effect; the remainder operates through a channel unobserved in the data, consistent with the reference-set compression emphasized in the aspirations literature. The results imply that the welfare accounting of energy poverty should extend beyond present consumption to the beliefs households hold about their own futures.

title: Household Demand Responses to Carbon Pricing by Energy Poverty Status: Evidence from Belgium
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Household Demand Responses to Carbon Pricing by Energy Poverty Status: Evidence from Belgium
detail.abstract: This paper examines how carbon pricing affects the welfare of energy vulnerable households in Belgium, distinguishing between energy poor (EP) households, who devote a large share of income to energy, and hidden energy poor (hEP) households, who severely restrict their consumption. Using eleven cross-sections of the Belgian Household Budget Survey (2003–2016), we characterise both groups through logistic regressions and estimate a demographically specified Quadratic Almost Ideal Demand System, developing a two-stage residual inclusion procedure to address the endogeneity of energy vulnerability status. The resulting group-specific price and budget elasticities are used to simulate the welfare impact of a carbon price on heating and transport fuels calibrated to the forthcoming EU ETS 2 (2028). Behavioural adjustments are heterogeneous: lower-income and energy vulnerable households exhibit higher fuel price elasticities than wealthier groups, with hEP households responding most strongly to price increases. The welfare analysis reveals that EP households face substantial carbon costs but comparatively modest welfare losses, whereas hEP households bear a disproportionate relative welfare burden despite their low expenditure-based exposure. These findings highlight horizontal equity concerns missed by income-based metrics and call for integrating energy vulnerability profiles and welfare measures into carbon pricing design.

title: Housing Tenure Model as an Institutional Condition -Baseline Comparative Profiles of Conditions, Wellbeing and Social Connection across Canadian Housing Tenure Models

detail.title: Housing Tenure Model as an Institutional Condition -Baseline Comparative Profiles of Conditions, Wellbeing and Social Connection across Canadian Housing Tenure Models
detail.abstract:
Cooperative housing occupies a unique position on the tenure spectrum between owning and renting, offering collective ownership, democratic self-governance, secure tenure, and affordability.  Despite growing interest in housing’s importance as a social determinant of health, cooperative housing has received very limited attention among housing researchers. This paper introduces a biopsychosocial (BPS) framework for housing that draws on Engel’s BPS model of health (1977) and Pearlin et al.’s (1981) stress process model to examine how the structure of the cooperative tenure model may reduce housing-related stressors and encourage social connection among residents. Using data from the 2018 Canadian Housing Survey (CHS), market cooperative residents are compared with those in market rental housing and other housing tenure groups across demographic characteristics, housing-related conditions and satisfaction, and well-being outcomes.

Results show that market cooperative residents experience significantly lower housing costs, longer tenure, greater economic buffering, and reduced exposure to housing-related stressors than private-market renters.  These advantages, however, are heterogeneous across household types.  Single-person cooperative households report substantially better mental health than their rental counterparts. In contrast, single-parent cooperative households report worse mental health outcomes, suggesting that the specific protective effects of cooperative models depend on household context.  These results provide descriptive evidence supporting a tenure-model-centered biopsychosocial approach to housing and health research and highlight household heterogeneity as a central consideration for both policy and future research.

title: Observable Matrix Dynamics of Stocks
affiliations: Fidelity Investments, Inc.

detail.title: Observable Matrix Dynamics of Stocks
detail.abstract: The Observable Matrix Dynamics (OMD) approach monitors the time development of complex non-linear systems through the trajectory of a fixed-size distance matrix and its spectrum. We apply it to the S&P 500 cross section over three crisis decades, the 2001 dot-com bust, the 2007-2008 financial crisis, and the 2020 Covid crash, with three fixed-size observables on a fixed universe. The arccos distance matrix of the rolling return correlations reads the correlation geometry: its effective dimension collapses at the 2008 and 2020 crises, while the 2001 bust is a dispersed unwind. Read against machine-learning distance matrices, its spectrum stays in the un-relaxed, pre-learning regime with no low-dimensional manifold, so the market never learns its correlation structure or relaxes to a stationary geometry. Subtracting the market factor exposes a coherent sector rotation, whose name-level attribution identifies which stocks drive each crisis and in what order. At a short lookback these signals resolve precursors and forecast the endogenous 2008 crisis, though not the exogenous 2020 shock. The other two observables model the daily return and volatility rankings as Markov chains on their ranking spaces. The return chain has persistent, defensive-led bellwethers and near-reversible dynamics. The volatility chain is far more persistent, led by the financial sector, and is the only one to carry a weak, episodic arrow of time, flaring at market stress and matching volatility clustering and the Zumbach effect. All three matrices show coherent changes during market crashes.

title: Addiction Beyond Autobiographical Memory: Implicit Learning, Craving, Habit, and Psychosocial Continuity After Autobiographical Memory Loss

detail.abstract: This article examines whether addiction-related vulnerability can persist after severe autobiographical memory loss. It argues that substance use disorder is not stored in autobiographical memory alone, but is sustained by partially dissociable systems, including implicit and procedural learning, conditioned cue reactivity, craving, withdrawal, interoception, habit, and social context. Autobiographical amnesia may therefore leave important dimensions of addiction intact, although focal damage to hippocampal, insular, or striatal circuits may also weaken craving or habitual drug seeking. Drawing on addiction science, memory research, neuropsychology, and psychosocial theory, the paper proposes a distributed continuity framework for understanding the persistence, transformation, or attenuation of addiction after memory loss. Assessment and care should not rely exclusively on autobiographical recall, but should also address bodily states, routines, environmental cues, and social support.

title: Temperature Shocks and Fertility: Evidence from Reproductive Preferences and Sexual Behavior
